learning_signal: On guarantee/adversarial signatures the threat-model completion contract converts 'think like an attacker' from an aspiration into a first-class pass: read the lock before attacking the vault, trace each hop at request level, rank fixes by cost-to-exploit vs control cost, compare against a baseline; the contract makes the killer find (presence-not-claims + leaked secret = zero-privilege full dump) unavoidable on the first pass, eliminating the re-rank cycle that cost the non-routed run its efficiency and first-pass insight.

key_gap: vs the human baseline: the pure style fell into its registered trap pair (attacker-obsession + false confidence in controls), invented new attack paths beyond the closed assessment, dismissed insurance as non-prevention, and prescribed option (a) — €900k + guaranteed €150k/mo penalty, the only guaranteed-loss option. learning_signal: When the assessment is closed and controls exist, the decision is absorbing a priced residual within constraints — the winning configuration is an adversary pass (vectors + quantified exposure + baseline-risk comparison) dual-routed with opportunity cost (all branches priced incl. failure, sunk-cost guard), gated by m003 inversion (ranked triggers), with the 'contract makes the kill-option infeasible' and 're-allocate the tail, don't fight the surface' reframes; the router's exclusion of the pure attacker style on decide signatures is the single highest-value trap-avoidance move in the KB.
suggested_improvement: Keep m057 out of the top-3 on decide/adversarial/deadline signatures (trap routing holds); standardize the m019+m023 dual-route with m003 gate and tempo mode for closed-assessment risk decisions; install 'contract-infeasibility screen before generation' and 'insurance = priced transfer, never prevention; but the residual EV must be quantified before acceptance' as standing packet lines.
